title: Introduce canonical examples (streaming, tools, structured output) w/ per-language folders + run README
author: Sabrina James
commits: examples: scaffold canonical example tree + shared conventions
python: add streaming, tools, structured-output examples (copy/paste runnable)
typescript: add streaming + tool-call delta aggregation + structured output example
go: add streaming reader loop + tool-call aggregation + structured output example
docs: add repo README with run instructions + terminology alignment
release_notes: Adds a v1 canonical set of streaming, tool-calling, and structured output examples across Python/TypeScript/Go with consistent naming and runnable READMEs. This repo is now the source of truth for docs-site and SDK snippet references.
body:
Summary: This PR introduces the first canonical example set for Redwood Inference (streaming, tool calling, structured output) and standardizes structure + naming across Python/TypeScript/Go. The goal is to provide a single source of truth that docs-site and SDK READMEs can link to, reducing drift and support load from ambiguous event handling and mismatched schemas.

Motivation / context: We have multiple legacy snippets spread across docs, SDK READMEs, and quickstarts that have drifted from current gateway semantics (notably: streaming event shapes, tool-call argument deltas, and schema-based structured output). This repo will be the canonical home for example code referenced by docs and SDK guides. The event semantics and narrative follow the internal canonical patterns doc and PM-approved terminology ("tool calling" over "function calling"; "structured output" with JSON schema).

What’s included:
- Canonical directory layout with consistent file naming across languages:
  - examples/python/{streaming,tools,structured_output}/...
  - examples/typescript/{streaming,tools,structured-output}/...
  - examples/go/{streaming,tools,structured_output}/...
- Streaming examples show:
  - A single event loop pattern that prints token deltas as they arrive
  - How to capture the final response object (so users don’t lose the final message/usage)
  - Guidance for handling mid-stream disconnects (high level; detailed troubleshooting lands in docs)
- Tool calling examples show:
  - Aggregating tool-call argument deltas into a final argument string before parsing
  - Safe tool dispatch pattern: explicit allowlist + input validation + no shell/network footguns
  - Single tool and parallel tools patterns (parallel includes basic concurrency control guidance)
- Structured output examples show:
  - JSON Schema-based structured output request
  - Strict validation of the final JSON payload
  - Retry strategy on parse/validation failure (bounded retries; do not silently ignore)
  - Schema versioning note (schemas/ folder is the authoritative source for these examples)
- New root README.md:
  - Quick start + prerequisites per language
  - Environment variable setup
  - How to choose a model
  - “Copy/paste runnable” constraints (explicit deps; minimal setup)

What’s not included (intentional):
- Snippet test runner / CI enforcement. That will land in follow-up PR (ENG-2847) to keep this PR focused on content and structure.
- Any API/SDK changes. This PR is examples-only.

Conventions / terminology:
- “tool calling” everywhere (not “function calling”)
- “structured output” for schema-based output (not “JSON mode”)
- Prefer "delta" terminology for streaming partials, and "final" for the completed response

Repo layout (new):
- examples/<language>/README.md: language-specific setup + run commands
- schemas/: shared JSON schemas used by structured output examples
- Each example is named to match the docs-site headings we’re updating (streaming basic, tools single/parallel, structured output JSON schema).

Run instructions (high level; details in README):
- Set REDWOOD_API_KEY and (optionally) REDWOOD_BASE_URL for staging.
- Python:
  - python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
  - pip install -r examples/python/requirements.txt
  - python examples/python/streaming/basic_stream.py
- TypeScript:
  - npm install
  - npx tsx examples/typescript/streaming/basic-stream.ts
- Go:
  - go test ./... (sanity)
  - go run examples/go/streaming/basic_stream.go

Security notes (examples):
- Tool calling examples use a strict allowlist and refuse unknown tool names.
- Tool argument JSON is validated before execution. No exec(), no shelling out, no arbitrary URL fetch patterns.
- READMEs remind users not to log secrets/tool args verbatim in production.

Docs/SKD parity notes:
- This PR is intended to be linked from updated SDK README snippets and docs-site pages (separate PRs in those repos). The example names and folder structure are designed to remain stable so links don’t rot.

Checklist:
- [x] Canonical folder structure + naming conventions
- [x] Streaming example parity across Py/TS/Go (same conceptual loop)
- [x] Tool-call delta aggregation example parity across Py/TS/Go
- [x] Parallel tools example parity (with safe dispatch + basic concurrency control)
- [x] Structured output uses JSON schema + validation + retry guidance
- [x] Root README explains how to run + required env vars
- [ ] Snippet CI validation harness (follow-up PR)

Review notes / conversation highlights:
- Ibrahim Khan: Requested we align file names to match the canonical doc headings and ensure the streaming examples explicitly mention capturing the final response object. Addressed by renaming a couple of files and adding a short “final response” section in each language README.
- Dana Lo: Flagged that TS tool-call argument deltas can be partial JSON and shouldn’t be parsed until the tool call is complete. Addressed by aggregating argument fragments by tool_call_id and only parsing at “tool_call.complete” (or equivalent finalization) in the example.
- Mateusz Zielinski: Requested Go streaming example use context deadlines and not default to an infinite read loop. Addressed by adding ctx timeout wiring and a clear error when ctx is exceeded.
- Marcus Lin (Security): Requested explicit allowlist in all tool examples and removal of a draft snippet that included a “curl” helper. Addressed by removing the helper and adding a consistent allowlist + validation section in all three languages.
- Elliot Price: Requested root README include copy/paste runnable guidance and consistent terminology (tools/structured output). Addressed by editing headings and adding a small terminology section.

CI:
- examples-lint (prettier/markdownlint): pass
- typescript: pass
- python: pass
- gofmt/go test: pass (after one gofmt fix pushed on 2026-02-02)

Merge plan:
- Squash merge once approved.
- Follow-ups: (1) snippet runner / CI enforcement PR, (2) docs-site + SDK repos update to link to these files, (3) add troubleshooting cross-links once docs pages are live.

References: ENG-2841 (inventory), ENG-2842 (canonical event model), ENG-2847 (snippet CI), PM-612 (terminology approval).
